title: Stateful testing: declare OpenAPI `links` + `operationId` so POST→GET→DELETE chains are exercised (currently 0 of 613 links covered)
description:
## Status update (2026-07-10) — the symptom changed, the gap did not

The original report said the **Stateful Testing tab is always empty** and zero scenarios run. That is **no longer accurate**, and the ticket has been rewritten around what a current sweep actually shows.

Schemathesis 4.x **infers** candidate links from path structure, so the stateful phase now executes. A full local sweep (2026-07-10, seed `3320112285`, Schemathesis 4.22.4) reported:

```
Stateful (in 26.37s)
  Scenarios:  110
  API Links:  0 covered / 613 selected / 613 total (613 inferred)
```

So: **110 scenarios ran, and 0 of 613 links were covered.** The phase is no longer silent — it is running and traversing nothing. The tab shows scenarios; what it does not show is a single completed resource lifecycle.

Two independent causes, both of which must be cleared before this ticket's acceptance criteria mean anything.

## Cause 1 — nothing is declared (this ticket)

The spec still declares:

* **0** `links` **objects** across 316 operations, and
* **0** `operationId` **values** (0 of 316).

Every one of the 613 links is *inferred* by Schemathesis from URL shape, not declared by us. Inference cannot know that `POST /api/documents` returns the `id` that `GET /api/documents/{id}` consumes, nor which of several candidates is the right chain. Declaring `links` + `operationId` is what turns 613 guesses into asserted lifecycle contracts.

This is also the part that benefits external consumers: `links` are how a spec tells a client "having created this, here is what you can do next".

## Cause 2 — writes cannot succeed today (blocked on [KS-428](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-428>))

A stateful chain begins with a successful POST. In the same sweep:

| POST outcome | Count |
| -- | -- |
| Total POST requests | 8,011 |
| `2xx` — resource actually created | **18** |
| `403 CSRF_TOKEN_MISSING` | **6,249** (78%) |
| other (4xx validation, etc.) | 1,744 |

The inverted CSRF guard in [KS-428](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-428>) rejects bearer-authenticated writes before they reach a handler. With 78% of POSTs blocked, **no amount of link declaration will produce a traversed chain** — there is no created resource to chain from.

**Sequencing:** [KS-428](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-428>) must land first, or this ticket's work cannot be verified. Declaring the links against a platform that refuses every POST would show `0 covered` exactly as it does now, and we would learn nothing about whether the declarations are correct.

## Fix

Add `operationId` to every operation in a chain, then `links` under each POST's success response, in the **source** `*.``openapi``.ts` registrations — not in `secuura-api.yaml`, which is generated and byte-compared by `npm run check:openapi` and so cannot be hand-edited.

```yaml
# Step 1 — operationId on each operation
paths:
  /api/documents:
    post:
      operationId: createDocument
  /api/documents/{id}:
    get:
      operationId: getDocument

# Step 2 — links on the POST success response
  /api/documents:
    post:
      responses:
        '201':
          description: Document created
          links:
            GetDocument:
              operationId: getDocument
              parameters:
                id: '$response.body#/data/id'
```

### Chains to implement

Three entries from the original table **do not exist in the spec** and have been removed: `POST /api/commitments`, `POST /api/proofs/generate`, `POST /api/disclosure/policies`. Verify each row against the spec before implementing — the list below is 26 POSTs, all confirmed present.

| POST (creates resource) | Response field | Downstream operations |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `POST /api/documents` | `data.id` | `GET /api/documents/{id}`, `POST /api/documents/{id}/anchor`, `POST /api/documents/{id}/verify`, `POST /api/documents/{id}/revoke`, `POST /api/documents/{id}/sign-cert`, `POST /api/documents/{id}/version` |
| `POST /api/credentials` | `data.id` | `GET /api/credentials/{id}`, `POST /api/credentials/{id}/revoke` |
| `POST /api/webhooks` | `data.id` | `GET /api/webhooks/{id}`, `PATCH /api/webhooks/{id}`, `DELETE /api/webhooks/{id}`, `POST /api/webhooks/{id}/test`, `POST /api/webhooks/{id}/rotate-secret` |
| `POST /api/timestamps` | `data.id` | `GET /api/timestamps/{id}` |
| `POST /api/timestamps/batch` | `data[*].id` | `GET /api/timestamps/{id}` |
| `POST /api/tenants` | `data.id` | `GET /api/tenants/{id}`, `PATCH /api/tenants/{id}`, `PATCH /api/tenants/{id}/status`, `DELETE /api/tenants/{id}` |
| `POST /api/issuer-certs` | `data.id` | `GET /api/issuer-certs/{id}`, `POST /api/issuer-certs/{id}/revoke`, `POST /api/issuer-certs/{id}/rotate` |

| `POST /api/governance/participants/register` | `data.id` | `GET /api/governance/participants/{id}` |
| `POST /api/oauth/apps` | `data.id` | `GET /api/oauth/apps/{id}`, `PATCH /api/oauth/apps/{id}`, `DELETE /api/oauth/apps/{id}`, `POST /api/oauth/apps/{id}/rotate-secret` |
| `POST /api/security/keys` | `data.id` | `DELETE /api/security/keys/{id}` |
| `POST /api/security/audit` | `data.id` | `GET /api/security/audit/{id}` |

| `POST /api/did` | `data.did` | `GET /api/did/{did}`, `PATCH /api/did/{did}`, `DELETE /api/did/{did}` |
| `POST /api/transfers` | `data.id` | `GET /api/transfers/{id}`, `GET /api/transfers/{id}/history`, `POST /api/transfers/{id}/approve`, `POST /api/transfers/{id}/reject`, `POST /api/transfers/{id}/execute`, `POST /api/transfers/{id}/cancel` |

| `POST /api/gdpr/dsr` | `data.dsrId` | `GET /api/gdpr/dsr/{dsrId}`, `PATCH /api/gdpr/dsr/{dsrId}` |
| `POST /api/referrals/generate` | `data.id` | `DELETE /api/referrals/{codeId}` |
| `POST /api/analytics/exports` | `data.id` | `GET /api/analytics/exports/{id}` |
| `POST /api/m365/sites` | `data.id` | `GET /api/m365/sites/{id}/libraries`, `DELETE /api/m365/sites/{id}` |
| `POST /api/m365/connections/init` | `data.id` | `GET /api/m365/connections/{id}`, `POST /api/m365/connections/{id}/refresh`, `DELETE /api/m365/connections/{id}` |

## Affected files

* The per-service `*.openapi.ts` registrations (source of truth)
* `Blockchain/Dev/docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml` — regenerated via `npm run generate-openapi`, verified by `npm run check:openapi`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] [KS-428](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-428>) resolved, so authenticated POSTs reach their handlers and a chain can begin.
- [ ] All 26 POST operations above have `operationId` set; all downstream operations referenced have `operationId` set.
- [ ] All 26 POST success responses declare `links` with the correct `operationId` and response-body pointer.
- [ ] `npm run generate-openapi` run; `npm run check:openapi` clean.
- [ ] A full sweep reports `API Links: N covered` with `N > 0` — the number that matters. "Scenarios ran" is already true today and is not evidence of a traversed chain.
- [ ] At least one complete create → read → delete lifecycle is visible in the report's Stateful tab.
- [ ] `python3 scripts/run.py quality` passes (0 errors); no regression on any existing passing check.

## Notes

* The original "0 of 329 operations" figure predates the current spec, which has **316 operations across 284 paths**. The `operationId` count is unchanged: still **0 of 316**.
* `links` and `operationId` are separate concerns from `x-workflows` (which Akto consumes). Declaring `links` does not affect Akto's scans.

## Related

* [KS-428](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-428>) — inverted CSRF guard. **Hard blocker**: 6,249 of 8,011 POSTs rejected, so no chain can form.
* [KS-256](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-256>) — OpenAPI inline examples (parallel work, same generated file)
* [KS-255](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-255>) — Request schema tightening (parallel work, same generated file)

**What was ruled.** Card `secuura-ks61-openapi-gaps-demote-1109`, option a: "Demote to Medium; KS-188 carries the operationId step".

**What this ticket already records.** Its own 2026-07-10 status update reads the spec as declaring "0 operationId values (0 of 316)" and "0 links objects across 316 operations". Its Fix section starts "Add operationId to every operation in a chain", while KS-61's step 1 is operationId on every operation. This comment does not say which of the two is the scope; that stays with the ticket's assignee.

**What this does not do.** It does not change this ticket's assignee, state or priority, and no code changes with it.

## Stateful `max-steps` measurement (from KS-1271 G, 2026-09-18)

Slot 1, Schemathesis 4.27.2, branch `feature/ks-1271-…` @ `e6b4c26d5`, `--phases stateful --max-examples 25 --workers 1`, scratch-dir copy of `schemathesis.toml` + `[phases.stateful] max-steps = N`; counted from the NDJSON (`ScenarioFinished` in phase `stateful`; steps = recorded cases; distinct ops = `METHOD path` across those cases). Links are still inferred (0 of 613 declared) — this measures the inferred chains only.

| max-steps | seed | scenarios | steps | distinct ops | failures | wall s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 6 (default) | 1271 | 71 | 551 | 73 | 2 | 25.0 |
| 6 | 1268 | 126 | 717 | 80 | 6 | 31.1 |
| 6 | 1170 | 32 | 229 | 44 | 0 | 10.6 |
| 10 | 1271 | 164 | 1578 | 112 | 8 | 72.8 |
| 10 | 1268 | 217 | 1725 | 108 | 14 | 75.2 |
| 10 | 1170 | 187 | 1608 | 109 | 12 | 74.1 |
| 15 | 1271 | 149 | 1504 | 113 | 11 | 66.0 |
| 15 | 1268 | 360 | 3856 | 141 | 23 | 170.6 |
| 15 | 1170 | 301 | 3162 | 142 | 19 | 144.0 |

Means — 6: 66 distinct ops / 22 s · 10: 110 / 74 s · 15: 132 / 127 s. 6→10 gives +67 % ops chained and collapses the seed-to-seed spread (44–80 → 108–112); 10→15 adds ~20 % for ~70 % more time with wide variance. No config change made under KS-1271; adopting a value is a decision for this ticket. The seed itself is not a lever (KS-1271 finding 6) — declared `links` remain the real one.

**Measured 2026-09-18 (KS-1268 bump sweeps, slot 1, head `52df64f84`) — how seed-dependent the stateful phase is with zero declared `links`:**

| run | Schemathesis | seed | stateful scenarios | steps | distinct ops chained |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `full` before | 4.27.1 | 3984995428 | 206 (96 empty) | 1,171 | 101 |
| `full` after | 4.27.2 | 799024034 | 62 (24 empty) | 479 | 60 |
| stateful-only, fixed seed | 4.27.1 | 799024034 | 104 (47 empty) | 558 | 76 |
| stateful-only, fixed seed | 4.27.2 | 799024034 | 73 (25 empty) | 548 | 74 |

Under a fixed seed the two versions chain the same amount (76 vs 74 ops, 558 vs 548 steps); across seeds the same version varies 2×+ in steps and 101 → 60 in operations reached. Every chain is inferred (`inference.algorithms = ["location-headers", "dependency-analysis"]`, the 4.27 default) because the spec declares none of its 613 links. The chain start also moves with the version's inference rules (4.27.2 accepts "collection nested under a parent" — `specs/openapi/stateful/dependencies/models.py`): 4.27.1 started 22 chains at `GET /api/governance/proposals/active`, 4.27.2 at `POST /api/m365/connections/{id}/refresh`.

Implication for this ticket: declaring `links` + `operationId` is what makes the stateful phase reproducible run-to-run, not a seed. Until then any stateful count in a report is a sample, not a measurement, and KS-1268-style before/after comparisons must fix the seed for that phase (done there; ~23 s per run).

## Results 2026-09-14 (Schemathesis 4.27.1) — stateful phase runs on inferred links, fails in 33.8 s, still 0 declared links

`full-2026-09-14T15-04-07Z-slot3` (the Mac, slot 3, from-scratch stack; `develop` @ `64c386e04` after the 4.27.1 bump; 342 ops, 0 errored, 22.3 min): the stateful phase executed on Schemathesis's *inferred* links, status **failure** after 33.84 s, with `not_a_server_error::Stateful tests` ×2 and `positive_data_acceptance::Stateful tests` ×1 — a 5xx and a rejected valid request reached inside inferred chains. The spec still declares no `links`, so this is inference finding whatever it can, not the POST→GET→DELETE contract this ticket is for.

Worth knowing for the fix: 4.27.0 added **dependency inference** (body fields linked to the collection listing their values; path parameters take values seen under the same name in earlier responses; values reused from list responses) — so the *inferred* coverage is broader than on 4.22.4, and the untriaged `positive_data_acceptance` set moved because of it (KS-591 / KS-1015). That is more reason, not less, to declare the real `links` + `operationId`s: inference now sends plausible chains the spec never promised, and a declared graph is what would let a stateful failure be attributed to a contract rather than a guess.

No change to this ticket's code. Refs as KS-NNN text.

## Hard measurement for this ticket: **`transitions: 0 of 318` with 104 producers available** — and it accounts for ~78% of the full sweep's failures

From the KS-544 full sweep `full-2026-08-05T08-44-00Z` (Schemathesis 4.24.3, 316/318 operations, 316/317 past auth). The engine's own `LoadingFinished` event reports:

```
operations:      {total: 318, selected: 316}
transitions:     {total: 0, selected: 0}     <- zero
producer_labels: 104
```

Schemathesis identifies **104 operations that can produce a resource** and **zero declared transitions to consume them**. This is the same fact as this ticket's "0 of 613 links covered", but stated from the other side and, I think, more usefully: it is not that the links fail to traverse — there are **no declared transitions at all** for the phase to attempt.

### Why it is worth quantifying now

`positive_data_acceptance` failed **751 times across 78 operations** in that sweep — **~78% of all 968 failing check results**. Those are overwhelmingly operations fuzzed in a state where the call cannot legally succeed, because nothing chained a create before them. The §11 ten (governance/transfers/referrals/stake/m365) are a *subset*; the pattern is far wider.

So this ticket is not one class among several — landing it should collapse the large majority of the sweep's reported failures in one move. Worth weighing when sequencing against KS-518 (153 results), KS-508 (8) and KS-565 (53).

### Two notes for whoever picks it up

- **Cause 2 in the description is no longer a blocker.** KS-428 is Done, and this sweep confirms writes reach handlers: 316/317 operations past auth, `POST` operations returning real 201s. The "78% of POSTs 403'd by CSRF" condition is gone, so option (a) can now actually be *verified* rather than showing `0 covered` for the wrong reason.
- **The measurement is cheap to re-take.** It is in every run's `schemathesis-output.ndjson` — the single `LoadingFinished` event. That makes it a clean acceptance signal for this ticket: `transitions.total > 0` is unambiguous, where "scenarios ran" is not.

I have also flagged surfacing this on the HTML report's Overview, since it is currently invisible there — a reader sees 78 failing operations rather than one contract gap.

*From the KS-544 sweeps, 2026-08-05.*

## Fallback path added here — option (b): publish the undeclared 409/422s (from KS-478)

Recording this on KS-188 so it has an owner, because **KS-478 is being closed** and this was the only place it lived.

KS-478 (*"KS-466 §11 — state-machine/precondition 400s: resolve via KS-188 stateful links, else publish the missing 409/422s"*) framed the §11 problem as a fork. Its **option (a)** — declare `links` + `operationId` — is entirely this ticket's scope and far better specified here. Its **option (b)** was not ticketed anywhere.

### Option (b), in full

Ten operations answer legitimate business-rule refusals that the sweep reports as `API rejected schema-compliant request`, because the fuzzer cannot chain create → submit → vote to reach a state where the call would be valid:

- `POST /api/governance/proposals/{id}/execute` · `/submit` · `/cancel` · `/vote`
- `POST /api/transfers/{id}/reject`
- `POST /api/referrals/apply`
- `POST /api/stake/unstake`
- `POST /api/m365/sites` · `POST /api/m365/documents/sync`
- `POST /api/governance/delegate`

Typical bodies: *"Only draft proposals can be submitted"*, *"Cannot reject transfer in executing status"*, *"Invalid referral code"*, *"Invalid or disconnected connection"*.

If `links` stay blocked, the alternative is to **declare those refusal statuses in the spec** — publish the genuinely undeclared **409/422** responses on each operation, in the source `*.openapi.ts` registrations, so the sweep stops treating a correct refusal as a contract violation.

### Why this matters more than it used to

This ticket is blocked on **KS-428** (inverted CSRF guard — 6,249 of 8,011 POSTs rejected 403), and option (a) cannot even be *verified* until that lands. If KS-428 isn't moving, **option (b) becomes the realistic path**, and it is cheap by comparison: a response declaration per operation, no chaining, no dependency on writes succeeding.

Option (b) is a **narrower** fix — it silences the false positives without giving the fuzzer real lifecycle coverage, which only (a) delivers. Worth doing (a) if KS-428 clears; worth doing (b) if it doesn't.

### The refusals are already proven correct

KS-478 shipped and merged the **verification leg**: `tests/test_state_machine_preconditions.py` drives each of the ten ops to its unmet precondition and pins the refusal to a clean, enveloped business 4xx — never a raw 5xx, never a silent 2xx. **10/10 exercised and passing** on the merged code, with its own report tab and runner gate.

So whichever option is chosen, there is already a regression suite proving these ten refusals *are* correct behaviour and the sweep's reports on them *are* false positives. That evidence is not lost by closing KS-478.

— PR #591, merged to `develop` 2026-07-24.

Unblocked as of 2026-07-11: the hard blocker **KS-428** (inverted CSRF guard rejecting bearer-authenticated writes) is now **Done** (PR #480). Authenticated POSTs now reach their handlers, so a stateful chain can actually begin and the `links` + `operationId` declarations in this ticket can be verified against a platform that no longer refuses every write. Ready to proceed. (Note: several write-path defects were unmasked once writes became reachable — KS-430 contract drift, KS-431 raw 500s, KS-439 content-type — worth being aware of when validating chains, though they don't re-block this work.)
